6. The instant application seeks grant of interim bail in proceedings emanating from FIR No.
76/2023 dated 13th January, 2023 registered under Section 363 of the Indian Penal Code, 18604 at P.S. Swaroop Nagar.
Subsequently, a chargesheet was filed qua the Petitioner under Sections 363/376/506 of IPC and Section 6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.5 7.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012.5
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
The Applicant was initially granted regular bail by the Sessions Court on 19th August, 2023,
subject to strict conditions, including a direction not to reside near the victim or establish any form of contact with her.
However, owing to an alleged breach of this condition, the Sessions Court, by order dated 26th March, 2025, cancelled his bail.
A subsequent application for regular bail was also rejected on 19th April, 2025.

8. A perusal of the record reveals that in her testimony recorded before the Trial Court on 4th April,
2025, the victim substantially contradicted the version set out in the FIR.

She expressly deposed that no physical relationship existed between her and the Applicant prior to the registration of the FIR, and that their consensual sexual relationship commenced only after 9th October, 2024, when she voluntarily chose to start living with him.

She further clarified that the complaint was filed at the behest of her family "IPC"
"POCSO"

Regarding the disbursement of interim compensation amounting to INR 2,67,000/- by the District Legal Services Authority, the victim candidly admitted to having signed the withdrawal form, albeit under her mother's coercion.
9. These admission are indeed grave and concerning.

The Sessions Court by order dated 19th April,
2025 rightly took cognizance of the victim's admission concerning the compensation and directed appropriate steps to the DLSA (North) for its recovery.
These directions appears well-founded given the circumstances that have now come to light.

10. As regards the Applicant's alleged breach of bail conditions, it is pertinent to highlight that prima facie the violation stems not from any wilful misconduct on his part but from the victim's voluntary act of joining and residing with him.
The victim's own testimony corroborates this sequence of events.

It has also been brought to the Court's attention that although no formal marriage ceremony has been performed, the victim is currently pregnant with the Applicant's child and is expected to deliver on 16th July, 2025.
In this backdrop, attributing the breach solely to the Applicant would not be just or equitable.

sentences.text: In view of the above circumstances, this Court is of the considered opinion that the Applicant deserves interim relief, particularly to safeguard the interests of the victim and the unborn child.

Accordingly, the Applicant is directed to be released on interim bail upon furnishing a bail bond in the sum of INR 25,000/-, with two sureties of like amount, to the satisfaction of the concerned Jail Superintendent/Trial Court/Duty Metropolitan Magistrate, subject to the following conditions:

(f) The Applicant shall not commit any offence during the period of his release.
12. With the above directions, the present application is disposed of.
13. A copy of this order also be sent to DLSA for necessary information.
